analysis.title: Will the US dollar's strength last?
key_insights: The US dollar index hit a 19-month high on 19 November on risk aversion from an AI stock sell-off and hawkish readings of recent Fed commentary.
DXY eased 0.2% to 103.6 on 23 November as US equity futures rebounded and markets priced out a 50bp December Fed hike.
Incoming PMI, core PCE, durable goods, GDP and consumer sentiment data may show resilience and support the dollar near term.
UBS expects growth to slow toward 2% in 2027 on tighter financial conditions, fading fiscal support and weaker wealth effects.
UBS expects disinflation from Q2 2027 to let investors temper rate hike expectations, softening the dollar.
Extended USD positioning is expected to unwind, removing a technical support.
Near term, investors can monetize higher volatility for yield or gradually cut excess USD exposure into strength.
Sterling is the preferred G10 currency for 2027, with diversified EM carry via MXN, ZAR, BRL and INR. CHF is expected to underperform on a total return basis.
UBS expects gold to rally toward USD 5,000/oz as US real yields and the USD decline. Q3 2026 central bank purchases rose 42% YoY to 321 tonnes and ETF inflows were 211 tonnes.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down 0.2% from a 19-month high hit on 19 November. Near-term strength is supported by risk aversion and rate expectations.
UBS expects deceleration, which would weaken USD support.
Reduced hawkish pricing pulled the dollar back from its high.
Supported by lower real yields, a weaker USD and central bank demand.

tension_points.bull_case: Risk aversion from the AI sell-off, hawkish Fed commentary and resilient incoming data may sustain USD strength near term.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth slowing toward 2%, disinflation from Q2 2027 tempering hike expectations, and extended positioning unwinding should weaken the dollar in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weaker data or a deeper deterioration in risk sentiment would break the near-term dollar rally, while disinflation from Q2 2027 would confirm the bearish turn.
